learn.title: Covering a solid
learn.body: Surface area is the total area of all the faces of a solid, measured in square units. It tells you how much wrapping paper or paint you need, while volume tells how much fits inside.

learn.title: Prisms and cylinders
learn.body: For a prism, add the areas of all faces. For a box: $2(lw+lh+wh)$. A cube with side $s$ has $6s^2$. A cylinder has two circles and one rolled-up rectangle: $2\pi r^2+2\pi rh$.

learn.title: Sphere and cone
learn.body: A sphere has surface area $4\pi r^2$, exactly four times the area of its great circle. A cone has a base $\pi r^2$ and a side area $\pi rl$, where $l$ is the slant height.
Picture the net, the solid unfolded flat. Surface area is the area of the net.

questions.prompt: Find the surface area of a cube with side 5.
Find the surface area of a box that is 4 by 3 by 5.
A cylinder has radius 3 and height 10. What is its surface area in terms of $\pi$?
questions.explanation: $2\pi r^2+2\pi rh=18\pi+60\pi=78\pi$. The $90\pi$ is the volume.

questions.prompt: The surface area of a sphere is $4\pi\_\_$.
questions.explanation: Surface area is measured in square units, so it uses $r^2$.

questions.prompt: A sphere has radius 5. Its surface area is $k\pi$. Find $k$.
Which measures how much paint covers a solid?
questions.explanation: Paint covers surfaces, so you need the surface area.

questions.prompt: A cone has radius 3 and slant height 5. Its side area is $k\pi$. Find $k$.
